intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a modal dialog that renders outside the normal React component hierarchy using React Portals. You'll learn how to create portals to render components at different DOM locations while maintaining React's event bubbling and context. The main technologies involved are React's createPortal function, TypeScript for type safety, and DOM manipulation. This beginner-friendly lesson will show you how to overcome CSS stacking context limitations and create cleaner component structures.
intro.usecase: Portals are essential for rendering UI elements outside the normal React component hierarchy while maintaining React's state and event handling. This pattern is commonly used for modal dialogs, tooltips, dropdown menus, and notification toasts that need to appear above other content. In real applications, portals enable features like login modals that overlay the main page, side panels that slide in from the edge, or date pickers that pop up over form fields. Developers use portals to manage z-index conflicts and ensure UI components render in the correct DOM location while keeping React's component structure clean.
